title: AI Engineering with the Google Gemini 2.5 Model Family - Philipp Schmid, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A hands-on Gemini 2.5 workshop covering text generation, multimodality, structured outputs, function calling, native tools (search/code execution/URL context), and MCP integration. It is mostly a product tutorial; the transferable parts are token/cost accounting, thinking-budget control, structured outputs, and MCP tool abstraction.

takeaways.what_they_do: Gemini 2.5 Flash is hybrid: setting thinking budget to 0 disables reasoning tokens (cheaper output rate), and budgets are tunable 0–24k tokens; they recommend sweeping budgets against an eval to find the accuracy/cost knee.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can run evaluation of thinking budget zero, 1,000, 2,000, 4,000 and see how it impacts your evaluation and then you can like calculate for yourself
takeaways.numbers: thinking budget integer 0–24,000; example request had ~639 thought tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: Every response exposes usage metadata (input, thought, candidate tokens); they compute cost per request from input vs output pricing rather than guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a usage meta data object includes all of our consumed tokens and generated tokens
takeaways.numbers: input vs output priced differently; output far more expensive

takeaways.technique: File/URI references instead of inlining blobs
takeaways.what_they_do: Upload large documents once via a Files API and pass only a URI reference in each request; the backend loads it into context, avoiding resending the file every call.
Automatic caching works from the beginning of the prompt; put the large stable document first and vary only the trailing prompt so the prefix stays cacheable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you put the the PDF in the beginning and change the prompt behind it, it should work

takeaways.technique: MCP session as tool source, cap tool count
takeaways.what_they_do: Pass an MCP session directly as the tools argument; the SDK runs the list-tools → call → feed-back loop. They warn tool counts above ~5–10 degrade selection and suggest embedding-based filtering of tool descriptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the suggestion is probably between five to 10 and um if you have more tools you can use embedding models to basically filter
takeaways.numbers: recommended 5–10 tools; users seen at 50–100 tools

takeaways.technique: Structured output schema for extraction tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Force model output into a Pydantic/JSON schema (response_schema); when the schema didn't match the document, the model returned an empty list instead of hallucinating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: So Gemini did not generate or hallucinated something. So we get back a empty recipe list
